questions.question_text: Which of the following studies estimated differences in the incidence of psychosis in different ethnic groups in UK?

questions.question_text: The majority of patients with mental health issues are seen in the community, with only a minority seen in specialised care. According to the model designed by Goldberg and Huxley, which of the following is found between the levels of the pathway of care?
questions.explanation: The Levels and Filters Model was originally designed by Goldberg and Huxley. The original model describes the pathway between community and specialised mental health (MH) care, with some events being considered filters to move from one level to the next. The first level is the existing morbidity in the community. The second level comprises all the people with MH issues that make contact with a primary care service, while the third level represents the group with conspicuous MH issues. The fourth level are the people that are referred to specialised MH care, and the last level is the group actually receiving specialised care. The path from community to specialised care has a series of filters: the decision by the patient to seek medical help; the recognition of a MH problem by the general practitioner (GP); the decision by the GP to provide care or refer to specialised care; the decision by the psychiatrist to provide care. The model highlights that the majority of patients with MH issues are seen in the first level, and a minority, consisting mostly of severe case, in the last levels.Ref: Amaral CE et al. Systematic review of pathways to mental health care in Brazil:narrative synthesis of quantitative and qualitative studies. International Journal of Mental Health Systems. 2018 Dec;12(1):1-4.

questions.question_text: In legal terms, which of the following regarding capacity is correct?

options.text: Capacity is a legal, not a medical, concept
There is nothing called presumed capacity
Capacity is generic and not task specific
Children are presumed to lack capacity by default
Written consent is required to demonstrate capacity

correct_answer.text: Capacity is a legal, not a medical, concept

correct_answers.text: Capacity is a legal, not a medical, concept

questions.explanation: Capacity is a legal concept. Incapacity law and common law in the UK presume capacity in adults. Capacity is not global but task specific. Capacity must be assessed in relation to the particular decision required of the person. A young person aged over 16 is presumed to have capacity to consent to treatment, while a child aged under 16 can consent if they are deemed competent. Capacity involves assessing whether the child or young person understands what the treatment or investigation is, why it is needed, the possible outcomes of treatment, and what could happen if they do not receive treatment. Capacity assessments are decision-specific.Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. pp. 653, 856, 936.

questions.question_text: ECT has good evidence for treatment of severe depression though the evidence for continuation ECT is scarce. What percentage of patients will relapse despite treatment with maintenance ECT for severe depression after initial positive response?
questions.explanation: ECT has time-limited action and with poor durability (i.e. after a response, most patients will relapse). The relapse rate without maintenance treatment is > 80% in 6 months after successful ECT. Relapse can be significantly reduced by pharmacotherapy or continuation/maintenance ECT. Despite this, the overall relapse rate remains 30-50%.Ref: Royal College of Psychiatrists. Statement on electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).2017.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a risk factor for child maltreatment?
questions.explanation: The highest rate of child maltreatment is among children less than one year of age.In general, the rate of confirmed maltreatment steadily decreases or remainsconstant as children age. Research also indicates that children with special healthcare needs or disabilities are at greater risk for maltreatment. Well-establishedfamily level risk factors for maltreatment include poverty, parental mental healthand substance use disorders, and intimate partner violence. At the communitylevel, risk factors include neighbourhood crime and violence and concentrateddisadvantage. At a societal level, specific economic policies and trends (such asregressive taxes and recessions) and gender inequality are risk factors for childmaltreatment.Ref: Austin AE et al. Risk and protective factors for child maltreatment: A review.Current epidemiology reports. 2020 Dec;7:334-42.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor for child maltreatment?
questions.explanation: Multiple studies consistently demonstrate associations of parental mental healthand substance use disorders and intimate partner violence (IPV) with childmaltreatment. Mothers who report IPV by a current partner are more likely toendorse physical and psychological aggression, spanking, and neglect. Indicators ofcommunity violence such as IPV, aggravated assaults, and drug crimes also predictincreases in confirmed maltreatment. Gender inequality, a well-established riskfactor for multiple forms of violence including sexual assault and IPV, may also be asocietal level risk factor for child maltreatment.Ref: Austin AE et al. Risk and protective factors for child maltreatment: A review.Current epidemiology reports. 2020 Dec;7:334-42.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has NOT been evaluated in the early intervention (EI) of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Outcomes for patients in early intervention (EI) services are better than for standard care within community mental health teams. EI services have lower caseloads, have better access to psychological and social support and treatment, and can work more intensively with patients and families. There is evidence that low-dose antipsychotic medication (such as risperidone or olanzapine), CBT, and/or supportive therapy can improve attenuated psychotic symptoms. Individual CBT can be considered as acceptable alternative to pharmacologic treatment. If antipsychotic medication is considered, prescriptions should be given by specialist psychiatric services such as an EI team.Ref: Neale A, Kinnair D. Early intervention in psychosis services. Br J Gen Pract. 2017 Aug 1;67(661):370-1.Barnes TR et al.
